sections.value:
**Security: block** at `f105c6c1547307c12ee760e7ea69772c0b38e687` (F139), graded under C33.

The new orphan flow does not export log contents. Its title is fenced, but other notice and fallback fields remain raw. PM confirmed these are required reader-facing rendering repairs under C33, not same-user isolation findings.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/daemon/src/background.rs | 1555-1575 | S197-001: orphan notice interpolates the owner identity and full log path without grammar rendering/fencing | 9/10 |
| 2 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/daemon/src/background.rs | 1578-1582, 1603-1625 | S197-002: Telegram fallback explanation interpolates prime/owner identities and refusal/error text raw | 9/10 |

## Rendering boundary

`settle_orphan` uses the existing bounded title fence. The same new string directly interpolates `job.owner` and `job.out_path`, then is persisted and sent either to the warm prime or to Telegram.

Job ids and log filenames are daemon-minted, and the log directory derives from operator configuration rather than a job's cwd. That makes their origin relevant to account trust; it does not make arbitrary stored/operator path text safe to join into daemon-authored prose. Legacy identity values and unusual path text can still carry line breaks or confusing framing.

The fallback adds raw owner/prime ids and either a refused receipt's reason or an error Display string. It persists that explanation before Telegram admission, but persistence does not sanitize the copied text.

Render every displayed seat with `render::seat`. Fence the log path and fallback diagnostic text with `render::caller_text`, retaining the originals only as operational data. Exercise hostile stored identity/path text and a refused-prime diagnostic through the actual emitted/persisted notice, not just the title helper.

C33 explicitly keeps safe rendering in scope because it protects models and humans from confusing text. After asking before blocking this boundary, PM confirmed the required rendering repairs and said they are already being prepared in round two.

**C33: same-user, out of scope** — local id pre-reservation, local identity claims, operator-environment manipulation and local adversarial races are not security blockers here.

## Telegram disclosure

The prime receives the notice's job title/id/outcome, owner id, absence duration/classification and log path. Telegram receives that notice plus routing/fallback explanation; its existing sender presentation can add owner identity and a recorded folder basename. It uses the configured operator chat, not a new caller-selected destination.

The new orphan record contains notice text and route. No command, event payload, capability or log-tail contents are placed in it or sent by this orphan path. A completion body may be assembled locally before the owner check, but orphan settlement does not use that body.

No forbidden disclosure was established merely from the deliberately configured operator notification. This is a rendering block, not an assumed privacy rule against sending the declared summary/path to the operator. Fencing does not scrub secrets deliberately placed into metadata or confer semantic trust on that metadata.

## Policy and evidence limits

The 60-second brake and 24-hour grace are separate. The route is recorded before admission; prime fallback is persisted before Telegram enqueue. Successful queue admission is followed by `notified`, so a later revive does not redeliver.

That is queue acceptance, not proof of human observation or exactly-once Telegram network delivery. New tests do not exercise hostile metadata/fallback rendering or every crash/retry boundary around admission and marking. No deployment or live settlement was performed here.

## Exact head and CI

Local/remote/GitHub heads agree; detached shared worktree clean; PR CLEAN. Own F139 commit `66cd688c3b3f2b1257e7abac91675b5d5f857da6` is followed by the frozen main merge.

CI [42535960274](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42535960274) tested merge `a25342e1982c373e5981b0924f360787fdfe6938`, with this head and main `3f9c6206cb49c20608573bdbdf1f23827ed4ba53` as parents. Its tree `9f13ef4b723add9cdb8b8af026a6a16219c7bff1` equals the reviewed head's tree.

JUnit artifact [13639441685](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42535960274/artifacts/13639441685) confirms 2,303 passing cases, no failures; the runner separately reports five skipped. Past-grace settlement, within-grace bounded rechecks, revive-after-settlement, command-job settlement and unknown-owner Telegram tests all executed successfully, along with the two adjusted revive/refusal tests.

Current Node/Rust/Delivers checks succeed. The three brake/grace mutant kills remain author claims, not independently executed security evidence.

No local builds/tests, mutations, hostile/live-system probes, credential reads, product edits or performance/deployment measurements.
